lines: I remember fighting something inside me and losing. You gave me another morning.
The cure struck true. I remember you standing on the right side of it.
You pulled me back when even my name felt far away.
I heard your voice through the fever before I knew whose it was.
The hammer sounds like work again instead of a threat.
I held a blade today without waking <shake>afraid</shake>.
Food tastes right, steel looks clean, and I feel like myself.
You saved more than a weaponsmith. You saved the person holding the hammer.
I can stand at the grindstone again without losing time.
Some victories are won without drawing a weapon.
I owe you every honest day I get after this.
My hands remember the forge even when my mind hesitates.
Thank you for staying close enough to help.
I walked through the village today and recognized every door.
The first clean ring of the anvil nearly brought me to tears.
I am alive, steady, and back at my bench. That is enough for today.
No repair I have made compares with what you did for me.
I remember who kept watch while I could not trust myself.
The cure gave me my work back, but you gave me my life back.
If you ever need a blade repaired, mine is the first hammer you ask for.
Your face rings like steel, but everything around it is smoke.
I remember wanting to bite, then wanting to breathe. You were there between them.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
The forge is familiar until I reach for the wrong tool.
Some memories return bright and others refuse to take shape.
Tell me again how long I was gone.
I know you helped, but the reason keeps slipping away.
The grindstone sounds right. The rest of the village still feels strange.
I remember <shake>fear</shake> before I remember what frightened me.
Faces come back before names, and that bothers me.
There are hours missing between the fever and waking.
Please do not hand me a weapon until my head clears.
I can still judge an edge. I cannot always judge a memory.
The cure worked faster than my thoughts did.
Your voice is familiar enough to trust for now.
I keep checking the bench to make sure nothing moved.
Let the memories return on their own. Forcing them only hurts.
I know where I am. I just do not always know when.
Ask me one question at a time.
I believe I owe you thanks. Give me time to remember all of it.
I remember you, and I remember being <shake>dangerous</shake>. Do not make me relive either too quickly.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Keep some space until my grip steadies.
I am not touching a weapon while part of me still expects to attack.
The forge smells familiar, but sudden noise sends me back there.
I remember the hunger too clearly.
Do not stand between me and the door.
Being cured does not erase every fear.
My hands shake around people I know I trust.
The hammer fell behind me and I nearly ran.
I want to thank you. I also need you to step back.
Let me choose when I return to the grindstone.
A closed workshop feels smaller than it used to.
I keep checking my teeth and hands like the sickness might return.
Set any blades out of reach before we talk.
I am not angry with you. I am afraid of myself.
If I go quiet, let the silence do its work.
The memories will dull with time. Today they are still sharp.
I will come back to the forge when I can trust my own grip.
